questions.question: enters, requires _______(4) much time and energy.
questions.solution:
We need to understand the difference between *to *and *too*. 

*To *is a preposition used to show the relationship between the subject and the other elements of the sentence. 

*I cannot deliver this package to the owner.*

*Too* is used to indicate the idea of something in excess. It refers to the excessive or extra amount of something. It can also mean also.

*I am too tired to go to the mall.*

*You are worried too. (Here, too means also)*

In the given sentence, we are looking for the word that will emphasize the excessive (extra) amount of time and energy involved.

*...enters, requires **too** much time and energy...*

Thus, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

Sneha said, “I am buying a gaming console today.”

options.text: Sneha said that she is buying a gaming console today.
Sneha says she was buying a gaming console that day.
Sneha say that she is buying a gaming console on today.
Sneha said that she was buying a gaming console that day.

questions.solution:
The correct sentence in indirect speech is** 'Sneha said that she was buying a gaming console that day.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• In Direct speech, the actual words of the speaker are quoted within quotation marks.
 
• In Indirect speech, we report someone else’s statement in our own words.
 
• When we change the speech from Direct to Indirect, we drop the quotation marks and use the conjunction '**that'** before the Indirect statement. We make suitable changes in tenses as well.
 
• A simple present becomes a simple past:
 
 
• Drinks --> drank
 
 
 
• A present continuous becomes a past continuous:
 
 
• Is drinking --> was drinking
 
 
 
• A present perfect becomes a past perfect:
 
 
• Has eaten --> had eaten
 
 
 
• A simple past becomes a past perfect:
 
 
• Ate --> had eaten
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Also, *am* **changes to** *was*, *today* **changes to** *that day, **now* **changes to** *then*, *tomorrow* **changes to** *the next day, *etc.
 
• So, keeping these points in mind, the sentence in the question, when changed from Direct to Indirect speech, becomes: *Sneha said that she was buying a gaming console that day.*

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

The boss made the assistant work late.

options.text: The assistant was made to work late by the boss.
The assistant is being urged to work late.
The assistant was make to work late by the boss.
The assistant is working late due to the boss.

questions.solution:
The correct sentence in passive voice is '**The assistant was made to work late by the boss.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the subject is *someone* that works on the object.
 
• A sentence is said to be in Active Voice when the subject performs the action.
 
• When the subject is being acted upon by the verb – it is Passive Voice.
 
 
• The sequence in Active voice – Subject + verb + object
 
• The sequence in Passive voice – Object + verb + Subject
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The meaning conveyed by the sentence in both voices will remain the same, only the sequence of the subject and the object (or the action) changes.
 
• Let us understand this through an example
 
 
• **Active Voice:** *She kept the book in the cupboard.*
 
• **Passive Voice:** *The book was kept in the cupboard by her.*
 
 
 
• Note that 'kept' changes to 'was kept'.
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice as somebody is the subject performing an action.
 
• The sentence when converted in Passive voice becomes:
 
 
• *The assistant was made to work late by the boss.*
 
 

*Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.*

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

A serious critic

P : meaning of a work of art

Q : has to comprehend the particular

R : content, unique structure, and the special
questions.solution:

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The sentence starts with '*A serious critic'*
 
• Hence the next part should refer to or talk about this *critic *in one way or another
 
• Out of **P, Q and R, **only ***'Q' ***talks about to the critic who '*has to comprehend...'*
 
• Logically, the next part should talk about that which the critic should comprehend. Thus **R**, which talks about the *'content, unique structure...' *is the logical successor.
 
• The adjectives used in **R **should refer to something (noun) which is provided by **P - ***'meaning of a work of art'*

**Thus the correct sentence is: ***A serious critic has to comprehend the particular content, unique structure, and the special meaning of a work of art*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The 26th of January was chosen (1)/ to commemorate the Purna Swaraj (2)/ declaration for the complete independence, of 1930. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **3**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at each part of the sentence:
 
 
• ***The 26th of January was chosen:***

 
 
• *​*** **This part is grammatically correct since the superlative article **'*the' ***is used to refer to a very special date in our country's history
 
 
 
• ***to commemorate the Purna Swaraj:***
 
 
• ***​***Here, the usage of the superlative article ***'the' ***to refer to ***Purna Swaraj ***is correct as it refers to a specific historical declaration
 
 
 
• ***declaration for the complete independence, of 1930:***
 
 
• ***​***The word *declaration *means a formal statement of something
 
• It is followed by the preposition *of*. Example: Declaration of freedom, declaration of love etc
 
• The part *'..., of 1930' *is used to convey that the declaration was made in the year 1930 and is grammatically correct
 
 
 
 

 

**The correct sentence is:** *The 26th of January was chosen to commemorate the Purna Swaraj declaration **of** the complete independence, of 1930.*
